items.title: [djangocms-moderation] djangocms-moderation: Moderation comments disclosed to non-participant staff via the admin changelist
items.summary: SummaryThe Django admin views for moderation comments (CollectionCommentAdmin and RequestCommentAdmin) render the full comment body but scope access only by an attacker-controlled id in the URL and Django's model-level view_*comment permission. They perform no per-object participant check. As a result, any authenticated staff user who holds the comment view permission can read the comments of any collection or moderation request — including ones they are not a participant of — simply by supplying the target object's id.Comments are documented and intended to be private to the participants of a collection (its author and the moderators assigned to its workflow). This advisory concerns a read/write authorization asymmetry: the write paths already enforced request.user == obj.author, but the read paths did not enforce any participant check.DetailsModerationRequest.user_can_view_comments() — the gate intended to protect comment reads (author or assigned moderator) — existed in the codebase but was never called by the comment admins. Neither CollectionCommentAdmin nor RequestCommentAdmin overrode get_queryset, and their changelist_view / changeform_view methods resolved the target object directly from the user-supplied id without an authorization check.The changelists are hard-scoped to a single collection / moderation request (they raise Http404 when no id is present), so the exposure is not "all comments at once," but any specific collection's or request's comments can be retrieved by iterating ids.list_display on both admins includes the comment message, so the full   body is disclosed directly in the changelist HTML.The individual changeform (.../<id>/change/) discloses the same content   via a direct URL.ImpactType: Information disclosure / broken object-level authorization (IDOR).Confidentiality: Comment contents of collections/requests the user does   not participate in are exposed. This can include sensitive internal editorial   discussion.Integrity / Availability: No impact — comment creation, editing, and   deletion already enforced author checks and are unaffected.Who is affected: Deployments where more than one team/group of staff   reviewers holds the view_collectioncomment / view_requestcomment   permission. A reviewer of collection A can read the comments of collection B.WorkaroundsRestrict the view_collectioncomment and view_requestcomment model permissions to trusted users only, and avoid granting them across teams that must not see each other's moderation comments. This does not fully close the issue but reduces the set of users who can exploit it. Upgrading is the only complete fix.RemediationUpgrade to djangocms-moderation 2.4.1.The fix adds a user_can_view_comments participant gate (author or assigned moderator) to both comment admins, enforced in changelist_view and changeform_view for both the collection and request comment models. A ModerationCollection.user_can_view_comments() method was added to mirror the existing ModerationRequest.user_can_view_comments(). Non-participants now receive an HTTP 403 (PermissionDenied).CreditReported via coordinated disclosure.Referenceshttps://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-moderation/security/advisories/GHSA-pj7p-238h-76pvhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-69139https://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-moderation/pull/374https://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-moderation/commit/a044d9c98c127454b73e8a8ada6e59aaa0a8f621https://github.com/django-cms/djangocms-moderation/releases/tag/2.4.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pj7p-238h-76pv

items.title: [mareforma] Mareforma: Unsigned Claims Can Be Promoted to REPLICATED via Missing Signature Enforcement in Convergence Path
items.summary: Summarymareforma 0.3.3 contains a critical integrity flaw in the REPLICATED convergence logic (_maybe_update_replicated_unlocked() in mareforma/db/core.py:1300-1319). The peer-selection SQL query that determines whether two independent claims "agree" on the same anchor does not verify that either claim carries a valid cryptographic signature from an enrolled validator key. Because rekor_enabled=False is the default and automatically sets transparency_logged=1 at insert time, every claim — signed or not — immediately satisfies the convergence precondition. An attacker with no Mareforma key can write an unsigned claim to a shared graph, cause it to converge with a legitimate signed peer claim, and have it promoted to REPLICATED status. The forged REPLICATED row is then returned by the default trust query (graph.query(min_support="REPLICATED")), allowing the attacker to inject false trust signals into any downstream consumer relying on REPLICATED as a multi-party endorsement guarantee.DetailsRoot cause — mareforma/db/core.py:1300-1319The convergence function _maybe_update_replicated_unlocked() selects peer claims using a SQL query that filters on status, unresolved, transparency_logged, and artifact_hash, but contains no predicate on signature_bundle or enrolled-key identity:# mareforma/db/core.py:1300-1319rows = conn.execute(    f"""    SELECT DISTINCT c.claim_id, c.generated_by    FROM claims c, json_each(c.supports_json) j    WHERE j.value IN ({placeholders})      AND c.claim_id != ?      AND c.generated_by != ?      AND c.support_level != 'ESTABLISHED'      AND c.status = 'open'      AND c.unresolved = 0      AND c.transparency_logged = 1      AND (          c.artifact_hash IS NULL          OR ? IS NULL          OR c.artifact_hash = ?      )    """,Once peer rows are collected, the sink at core.py:1324-1334 promotes all matching claim IDs — including the attacker's — to REPLICATED without any additional validation.Why the preconditions are trivially satisfiedtransparency_logged = 1 is set automatically. When rekor_enabled=False (the library default), core.py:1061 sets transparency_logged = 1 immediately after insert. There is no Rekor step, so every claim becomes convergence-eligible the moment it is written.require_signed=False is the default. mareforma/__init__.py:41 defaults require_signed to False. When the attacker opens the graph with a non-existent key path, __init__.py:132-138 silently sets signer = None, enabling unsigned claim insertion.assert_claim() performs no signature gate. _graph.py:284-291 only validates DOI resolution on the supports list before forwarding attacker-controlled fields to _db.add_claim() (_graph.py:373-380).Why the forged claim surfaces in trust queriesThe default query path at core.py:3647-3650 filters out only PRELIMINARY claims whose generator is not enrolled. Claims at REPLICATED status are returned unconditionally, so the unsigned forged row is indistinguishable from a legitimately converged row in any downstream consumer.The helper that should have been calledcore.py:3661-3669 contains _extract_signature_bundle_keyid(), which can extract the key ID from a signature_bundle. This helper exists but is never invoked on the convergence path, indicating the validation was inadvertently omitted rather than a design decision.Complete data flow (source → sink)StepLocationDescription1cli.py:700-739CLI accepts arbitrary TEXT, --supports, --generated-by; lines 720-723 explicitly permit unsigned graph mode2__init__.py:128-138Missing key file → signer = None (no error raised)3_graph.py:284-291assert_claim() forwards user-controlled supports after DOI check only4_graph.py:373-380Calls _db.add_claim() with attacker-controlled claim fields5db/core.py:1208-1214Post-insert convergence triggered when unresolved == False and transparency_logged == 16db/core.py:1300-1319Peer-selection SQL — no signature_bundle or enrolled-key check (vulnerable sink)7db/core.py:1324-1334Updates peer and attacker claims to REPLICATED8db/core.py:3647-3650Default query returns REPLICATED rows without signature validationPoCPrerequisitespython3 -m venv /tmp/mareforma-poc/tmp/mareforma-poc/bin/pip install mareforma==0.3.3Or run the fully self-contained Docker image:# Build (from the repository root, with the local repo mounted under ./repo)docker build -f vuln-001/Dockerfile -t mareforma-vuln001 .# Run (no network required)docker run --rm --network none mareforma-vuln001Step-by-step attack#!/usr/bin/env python3from pathlib import Pathfrom tempfile import TemporaryDirectoryimport mareformafrom mareforma import signingwith TemporaryDirectory() as td:    root = Path(td)    key_path = root / "root-key.pem"    # Step 1: Legitimate root agent bootstraps a key and creates an ESTABLISHED anchor.    signing.bootstrap_key(key_path)    with mareforma.open(root, key_path=key_path) as g:        anchor = g.assert_claim(            "established anchor",            classification="DERIVED",            generated_by="seed/root",

items.title: [mareforma] Mareforma: transparency_logged trusts the unsigned rekor block
items.summary: What's wrongDuring restore, transparency_logged is recomputed as 1 if (toml_logged is not False and bundle_has_rekor) else 0, where bundle_has_rekor comes only from a rekor.uuid field inside signature_bundle. That derivation is wrong in both directions.First, the rekor block is metadata attached after signing (attach_rekor_entry in mareforma/signing/rekor.py leaves the payload and signatures untouched), so it is not covered by the Ed25519 signature. A hand-edited claims.toml can add "rekor": {"uuid": "x"} to any claim's bundle and forge the "publicly witnessed by Rekor" state. The claim signature still verifies, and restore never cross-checks the block against [rekor_inclusions] or the log. Tampering with claims.toml is the exact threat model restore defends against; _verify_claim_signatures_on_restore checks only payload and signatures.Second, a signed claim in a graph that never used Rekor is written with transparency_logged=1 (the column default when Rekor is disabled) but restores as 0 because its bundle has no rekor block. The convergence gate requires transparency_logged = 1, so post-restore peers can no longer converge to REPLICATED. With no rekor_url configured, refresh_unsigned() is a no-op and the flag stays 0 forever. Observed on the honest path: signed non-Rekor claim restores from transparency_logged=1 to 0, and a subsequent peer stays at PRELIMINARY instead of converging.Severity and impactHigh. An attacker who edits claims.toml can mark claims Rekor-witnessed and REPLICATED-eligible without them ever having been logged. Meanwhile the common honest configuration (signed, no Rekor) has its trust state silently degraded by every catastrophic-loss restore, with no recovery path.Locationmareforma/db/restore.py:376 reads toml_logged from the TOML and probes the bundle for a rekor.uuidmareforma/db/restore.py:385 computes resolved_transparency from the unsigned rekor block alonemareforma/db/core.py:1401 the REPLICATED convergence gate requires c.transparency_logged = 1Fix directionDo not derive transparency_logged from an unsigned envelope field. When a rekor block is present, require a matching, cryptographically verified [rekor_inclusions] entry (via verify_rekor_inclusion against the pinned log public key) whose hashedrekord spec.data.hash equals the SHA-256 of the claim's signed payload before setting 1; otherwise set 0.When the claim is signed and neither the bundle nor the graph carries Rekor coordinates, restore the write-time value: the TOML omits transparency_logged unless it was 0, so treat an absent flag plus no rekor bundle as 1 (the column default for non-Rekor writes).Do red/green TDD: add a regression test that fails on main, then make it pass.Quality barSOLID, DRY, KISS. Clean, readable, well-tested code. No new errors, warnings, or test failures; the full suite stays green on all supported Python versions.Referenceshttps://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/security/advisories/GHSA-xfq4-8hf9-5h43https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-71534https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/pull/58https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/commit/cccbf4eafd3c34b20b1686f12c0cad76c87566aehttps://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/releases/tag/v0.3.8https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xfq4-8hf9-5h43

items.title: [mareforma] Mareforma: invalidated claims still promote to REPLICATED
items.summary: What's wrong_maybe_update_replicated_unlocked never checks t_invalid, so a claim that a signed contradiction verdict has marked invalid can still climb to REPLICATED through convergence detection, and it pulls an honest peer up with it.Three gaps line up:The new-claim short-circuit reads only status and asserter_keyid (core.py:1339-1352); an invalidated but still-open new claim passes.The candidate-peer SELECT filters status = 'open', unresolved = 0, and transparency_logged = 1 but has no t_invalid predicate (core.py:1390-1410), so an invalidated existing claim qualifies as a convergence partner.The promotion UPDATE gates only on status = 'open' (core.py:1422-1426), leaving a TOCTOU window even after the SELECT is fixed.A signed contradiction verdict is meant to be terminal for the trust ladder: validate_claim refuses to promote a t_invalid claim to ESTABLISHED, and record_replication_verdict already gates its promotion UPDATE on t_invalid IS NULL. Convergence promotion is the one path that ignores the verdict. Reproduced at runtime: contradict claim X (t_invalid set, still PRELIMINARY), then assert peer Y sharing X's ESTABLISHED anchor; both X and Y land at REPLICATED, with X's t_invalid still set.Severity and impactHigh. A refuted claim re-enters the trust ladder at REPLICATED after its contradiction, and it serves as the corroborating peer that promotes an honest claim. Both outcomes contradict the documented refutation model, and REPLICATED is the input to further validation.Locationmareforma/db/core.py:1339 new-claim short-circuit checks status and asserter_keyid but not t_invalidmareforma/db/core.py:1390 candidate-peer SELECT WHERE clause has no t_invalid IS NULL predicatemareforma/db/core.py:1422 promotion UPDATE gates on status = 'open' only, reopening the window between SELECT and UPDATEFix directionTreat t_invalid the way the neighboring code already does. Extend the new-claim short-circuit to also read t_invalid and return when it is set. Add AND c.t_invalid IS NULL to the candidate-peer SELECT. Add AND t_invalid IS NULL to the promotion UPDATE's WHERE clause so the row-level lock closes the TOCTOU window, matching the gate record_replication_verdict already applies at core.py:3539.Do red/green TDD: add a regression test that fails on main, then make it pass.Quality barSOLID, DRY, KISS. Clean, readable, well-tested code. No new errors, warnings, or test failures; the full suite stays green on all supported Python versions.Referenceshttps://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/security/advisories/GHSA-rgg9-956j-3378https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-71500https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/pull/58https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/commit/c9d8922132d916e4fd013890cb4e17921e00065ehttps://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/releases/tag/v0.3.8https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgg9-956j-3378

items.title: [mareforma] Mareforma: verify_bundle never checks a per-claim signature
items.summary: What's wrongverify_bundle documents that it verifies "a bundle's DSSE envelope AND each per-claim signature", lists "per-claim signature failure" among its raised errors, and promises that partial verification never surfaces "an authenticated bundle that contains some invalid claims" as success. The code does not do this. The JSON-LD predicate built by JSONLDExporter._claim_node carries no signature material (there is no signatureBundle field on the node), so the verify loop has nothing cryptographic to check per claim. It only re-derives each claim's canonical-statement digest from the node fields and compares it to the signed subject list:chain_input = _signing.canonical_statement({...node fields...}, node.get("evidence") or {})expected = hashlib.sha256(chain_input).hexdigest()if subjects[subject_name] != expected:    raise BundleVerificationError(...)That digest check is self-referential: the exporter signs both the subject digests and the predicate nodes with the same key. It confirms the bundle is internally consistent as built, not that each claim's purported asserter ever validly signed it. The existing test test_tampered_claim_text_in_predicate_fails asserts a "digest mismatch", confirming digest-only verification is the actual contract.Severity and impactMedium. All trust in a bundle collapses to the single exporter key. Whoever holds it (or a malicious exporter) can emit a bundle containing claims whose asserter signatures are missing, invalid, or forged, and verify_bundle returns success. A relying party reading the docstring believes per-claim authenticity was verified when it was not. Security-sensitive because this is the trust boundary the SCITT-style export exists to provide.Locationmareforma/export_bundle.py:20 module docstring claims verification checks "every per-claim signature inside predicate"mareforma/export_bundle.py:183 verify_bundle docstring promises per-claim signature verification and a per-claim signature failure errormareforma/export_bundle.py:254 verify loop only recomputes and compares canonical-statement digestsmareforma/exporters/jsonld.py:178 _claim_node emits no signature field, so the predicate carries nothing to verify per claimFix directionTwo honest options. Either export each claim's signature bundle in the JSON-LD predicate and have verify_bundle cryptographically verify it (including the claim_id and subject binding) against the claim's asserter or validator key, raising on the first failure as documented. Or, if per-claim verification is out of scope for the bundle format, correct the module docstring and the verify_bundle docstring to state exactly what is verified: the bundle-level DSSE signature plus internal subject-digest consistency, with per-claim asserter signatures explicitly not checked.Do red/green TDD: add a regression test that fails on main, then make it pass.Quality barSOLID, DRY, KISS. Clean, readable, well-tested code. No new errors, warnings, or test failures; the full suite stays green on all supported Python versions.Referenceshttps://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/security/advisories/GHSA-hxh5-gp44-rc6phttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-71536https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/pull/58https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/commit/20caa4a5a9557a140a09a5d2c1c4a6a2124c0cc3https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/releases/tag/v0.3.8https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hxh5-gp44-rc6p

items.title: [mareforma] Mareforma: search_claims skips verify-on-read, serving forged rows
items.summary: What's wrongsearch_claims never calls _row_verified_on_read. Its row loop applies only the PRELIMINARY-unenrolled filter, then appends the row. query_claims runs the same projection but additionally re-verifies REPLICATED/ESTABLISHED signatures on read (line 4023) and drops any row that fails, per the documented tamper guarantee in the comment block above it: a high-trust row whose signature does not verify is excluded from query results entirely.So a tampered or forged high-trust row splits the two read paths. Any process with DB write access, or an attacker copying a genuine validation envelope onto a fresh row, can flip a row to ESTABLISHED. query() drops it; search() serves it at its persisted trust level. Verified in a runtime check against a forged ESTABLISHED row:query() returns forged row: Falsesearch() returns forged row: True   # support_level ESTABLISHED, 'verified' key absentThe docstring makes this worse: search_claims promises "the same projection as query_claims" and that the include_unverified filter "applies identically", so callers reasonably trust search results equally. The forged row also lacks the verified key entirely, so a consumer cannot tell it went unchecked.Severity and impactHigh. The verify-on-read tamper exclusion is a stated trust guarantee, and search is a primary read surface. A forged ESTABLISHED finding that query correctly rejects is served by search as genuine, with no marker that verification was skipped.Locationmareforma/db/core.py:4206 search_claims row loop applies only the PRELIMINARY-unenrolled filter, then appendsmareforma/db/core.py:4114 search_claims signature and docstring, which claims query_claims-identical semanticsmareforma/db/core.py:4023 query_claims verify-on-read call that search_claims lacksFix directionMirror query_claims: add a verify_cache: dict = {} and, inside the search_claims row loop after the include_unverified check, drop rows that fail _row_verified_on_read(conn, d, verify_cache). Since the verify filter can drop rows even when include_unverified=True, remove the single-batch break on include_unverified and keep batching until limit survivors or the FTS5 match-set is exhausted, with the same scan ceiling query_claims uses. Also set single_trust_domain / trust_domain_root on surviving ESTABLISHED rows if the "same projection" promise is to hold.Do red/green TDD: add a regression test that fails on main, then make it pass.Quality barSOLID, DRY, KISS. Clean, readable, well-tested code. No new errors, warnings, or test failures; the full suite stays green on all supported Python versions.Referenceshttps://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/security/advisories/GHSA-m29v-3g7g-9c63https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-71533https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/pull/58https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/commit/8b5291792128326a22f240123659d2754446c194https://github.com/mareforma/mareforma/releases/tag/v0.3.8https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m29v-3g7g-9c63
